claim: Every installed workstation unit's `ExecStart` names one module inside `.git/trees/service-workstation`, a worktree the deploy pins at the commit it last put up. Any landed folder move respells the checkout but cannot respell that worktree, which the change machinery never reaches, so from the moment a move lands until the worktree advances every unit names a file the worktree does not hold. That window opens for every move, by any seat. What makes it unclosable from inside is that the service advancing the worktree, `workstation-deploying`, launches through that same module and runs the deploy out of that same worktree. The 13.5-hour fleet outage of 2026-09-12 is one instance; the window is the finding.

evidence:
One path behind every unit. All 50 `.service` files under `/var/home/walton/.local/state/workstation-services/` carry the same `ExecStart`, differing only in the trailing slug: `/usr/bin/env bash -c 'exec bun /var/home/walton/repos/akasha/.git/trees/service-workstation/infrastructure/service/workstation/modules/service-running/service-running.module.code.ts <slug>'`. Nothing per-service is spelled on a page. `service-reading.module.code.ts:23` holds `RUNNER = "module/service-running"` and `:78` composes every start through `commandOf(root, { code: RUNNER, arguments: [slug] }, codeAt)`; `run-composing.module.code.ts:115` is the `join(codeAt, run.path)`; `service-putting-up.module.code.ts` passes `codeAt` down; `unit-writing.module.code.ts:53` writes the line. The design says so: `service-putting-up.module.ts:16-19`, 'The code a unit runs is spelled under the tree the deploy pinned rather than under the checkout.'

What advances the worktree. `deploy-tree-pinning.module.code.ts:11` names the path and `:19` moves it with `git reset --hard`, which is what the worktree reflog records. Its only caller is `deploy.command.code.ts`, so `akasha deploy` is the one thing that advances it. On a schedule that command is reached only through the `*-deploying` services, which launch through the shared module like everything else, and `deploy-looping.module.code.ts:93` then runs the deploy CLI at `join(tree, run.path)`, out of the same worktree. The repair path sits inside the window twice over.

What a move can reach. `move-folder.change-mechanical-folder.ts:42` repoints a body outside the folder naming a path that moved, `:84` does the same for manifests, `:88` takes the manifests from the index, `:133` judges the listing against the files git tracks. All of it is rooted at the checkout. Ripgrep over `/var/home/walton/repos/akasha/changes/` finds no mention of `.git/trees` or the `TREES` constant anywhere; the only users of that constant are deploy tree-pinning, `code-moving` and `index-surface`. The worktree is a checkout the change does not own, and the move is correct not to touch it.

The instance. `ff5b390b9e4` ('nest module pages under a modules folder', 2026-09-12T18:02:07-06:00) renamed `infrastructure/service/workstation/service-running/` to `.../modules/service-running/`; `git show --name-status` reads `R097` on the `.module.code.ts`. The worktree reflog shows `reset: moving to de2fb2952c7` at 17:58:19, four minutes and one commit before the rename, then no entry at all until `8cc618a4d3c` at 2026-09-13T07:33:11, 13h35m later. Units still named the old path at 18:02:04, where a `send-due-reminders` stack trace reads `.../workstations/service-running/service-running.module.code.ts`; a `systemctl` daemon-reload from a tmux scope follows the rename at 18:02:08; from 18:03:00 every unit that ran exited in milliseconds with `error: Module not found "...modules/service-running/service-running.module.code.ts"`. Thirty-one distinct units are logged doing so before 07:33, `audit-running` and every `*-deploying` service among them.

The deadlock in the journal. `workstation-deploying` last succeeded at 17:58:29 — 'put `service-workstation` up at de2fb2952c7', ten seconds after the reflog entry it wrote — then failed on the same `Module not found` at 18:03:00 and every minute after. It could not advance the worktree because it could not start, and it could not start because the worktree was behind. Recovery came from outside the loop: the reflog resumes at 07:33:11 and the two-minute cadence is back by 07:52.

The state has a name in the code already, for the adjacent case only. `run-composing.module.code.ts:116` refuses to compose a command whose file is absent under `codeAt`, saying 'the tree is behind the pages'. That did not prevent this render, and nothing refuses or reports the window itself.

No pending trigger for this particular move: on 2026-09-13, `git ls-files '*.module.code.ts'` filtered to folders not under `modules/` or `.server/` returns 0 of 6339, tree-wide and under `infrastructure/` alone. That narrows the next occurrence of this one rename, not the window, which any move reopens.

Why this is not the symlink finding. `a-folder-move-dangles-the-akasha-symlink-because-nothing-in-the-change-repoints-it` reasons about this hazard shape and files it as absent, on the premise that '35 units hold 35 paths of their own and a move breaking one breaks one'. The symlinks in `~/.config/systemd/user/` were never dangling here — each resolves to a file in `~/.local/state/workstation-services/` that exists. The dangle is one level down, inside the worktree the `ExecStart` reaches. Its single point is a hand-run provisioning symlink, replaceable from anywhere; this one is a deploy-advanced worktree that the service launching from it cannot advance. Distinct too from `a-folder-move-stops-the-service-whose-page-spells-the-moved-path` and `a-workstation-services-runs-path-is-never-checked-against-the-checkout`, both about a `runs` path spelled as stale data on a page: here the path is right against the checkout and wrong only against the tree.
